FILES: src/agents/pre-merge.ts (NEW) — the deterministic pre-merge signal engine: six families returning {from, into, signal, evidence} — (1) transliteration-identical slugs (the input language's digraphs collapsed from the language map itself, da/no oe/ae/aa→o/a/a; AUTO tier), (2) exact alias match (candidate title === another's frontmatter alias AND slugifies to its slug; AUTO tier), (3) corpus `Full Name (ABBR)` mining (capitalization-bounded so 'Data hentes fra Landspatientregisteret (LPR)' yields the right name; ABBR letters a subsequence of the name's letters), (4) edit-distance ≤2 on ≥10-char slugs (digit-only-diff and <50%-prefix-overlap guards), (5) token subsequence (≥2 tokens on the shorter side, org-unit-word/pure-digit extras blocked) + initials alignment (letter-only initials plus a required name-token↔initial alignment — morten-moller ✗ peter-moller and topic-a ✗ topic-b never fire), (6) formulaic families (region X/X-region/region-X cores; indikator-N bare/name↔name pairing that never pairs differing names) and a checked-in ~30-group da↔en domain glossary. Two tiers: AUTO-APPLY is exactly transliteration+alias (AUTO_APPLY_SIGNALS), everything else propose-only; neverMerge and vetoSlugs (splits) move auto-tier pairs to `vetoed`. src/state/curation-decisions.ts (NEW) — `.state/curation-decisions.json` {decisions: [{concern, action: merge|drop|cluster, from, into?, signal|model, decidedAt, runId}], splits: [slug]}; read creates it empty when absent (journalist discovers the knob), malformed → warning + empty; append dedupes by record key, backs corrupt bytes up to curation-decisions.corrupt.json, and CONSUMES split slugs touching a newly applied record (consumption keys off the pre-dedupe applied set so a re-merge of a split pair consumes the split). src/agents/curation.ts — CurateCallOptions.proposedPairs (ProposedPair imported from pre-merge), the prompts' PROPOSED PAIRS section filled by formatProposedPairsBlock and stripped byte-identically by stripProposedPairsBlock when empty, the additive "pairs" output parsed (justification capped at 120 chars) and validated (judgments must copy a proposed pair exactly, at most once; proposed-pair slugs rejected from merge/drop/keep/unsure buckets; confirmed pairs join the union-find merge edges with neverMerge vetoes intact; unjudged pairs are denials), verdicts surfaced as CurationOutcome.pairVerdicts (optional — all pre-existing stub literals compile unchanged); proposed pairs judged in exactly ONE call (the single call, or the reconciliation on the two-round path) and bucketCandidatesSized gains signal-aware grouping (pair-edge components pack as units; BYTE-IDENTICAL to the Phase 16 algorithm when no pair edges exist — gates 14.12/16.10 stay green). prompts/curation-entities.prompt.txt + curation-topics.prompt.txt — slot-additive: the 'Proposed pairs:' task block, the === PROPOSED PAIRS ===\n{proposedPairs}\n=== END PROPOSED PAIRS === section after END CANDIDATES, and the "pairs" output array; LF endings preserved; gates 14.13/16.9 prompt contracts untouched and still green. src/state/curation-report.ts — additive optional fields (legacy shape frozen): per-concern fromSticky, decidedThisRun (merges with signal+evidence, drops, denials), proposedPairs, autoApplied, top-level splitReversals; concern vetoes now sourced from the summary so auto-tier vetoes are recorded too. src/materializer.ts — the stage is now sticky → detect → auto-apply → propose → model: (1) `.state/curation-decisions.json` pre-applied BEFORE candidate construction (collapseStickyMerges union-find over active records; splits slugs and neverMerge pairs un-apply their records into splitReversals; sticky drops removed; manual-edit veto shared by every tier), so the model judges only unstuck candidates and a merged-away page can never reappear; (2) detectPreMergePairs per concern with document-page text as the abbreviation corpus (entity candidates now carry aliases from merged variant titles ∪ on-disk frontmatter aliases — readOnDiskEntityMeta reads them); (3) the AUTO tier applies with no LLM call through the SAME merge-application closures as model merges (one applyEntityMergeToMaps/applyTopicMergeToMaps pair shared by all three tiers); (4) proposed-pair members leave the open candidate list and ride the curation calls' proposedPairs; (5) every applied decision appended to the decisions file with its signal (auto → the signal, confirmed → the pair's signal, open model merges/drops → 'model'; runId = the report's run timestamp, hoisted so report and records share it). CurationSummary gains fromSticky/autoApplied/proposedPairs/denials/splitReversals; the report distinguishes fromSticky vs decidedThisRun with per-merge provenance. scripts/launcher-entry.ts — VERSION 1.0.5 → 1.0.6 with the dated comment (curation prompts are extracted assets; root AGENTS.md dist/ rule). tests/phase-21.test.ts (NEW) — gates 21.1–21.8 + supplementary (decisions-file contract; signal-aware bucketing with pairs judged in the reconciliation call). DESIGN DECISIONS A VERIFIER SHOULD KNOW: (a) Splits VETO the auto tier (vetoSlugs): a split survivor's accumulated frontmatter aliases would otherwise instantly re-merge the pair through the alias signal (caught by gate 21.7 during development) — the pair returns to the OPEN candidates and open discovery may still merge it, which consumes the slug; a permanent veto belongs in curation-overrides.json neverMerge. (b) A pair vetoed at the auto tier (neverMerge or splits) is reported in vetoes and NOT proposed (the human's veto is absolute for that run). (c) Family precision order: transliteration, alias, abbreviation, edit-distance, region-form, indicator-form, subsequence, initials, glossary — first edge wins a duplicate pair (an indikator-N-* pair records as indicator-form, not subsequence). (d) The edit-distance guard rejects digit-only differences (indikator-2 ✗ indikator-3) and low-prefix-overlap pairs (ct-skanning ✗ mr-skanning); s-creatinin/p-creatinin-class pairs fall to the model by design (precision over recall — the phase doc's mandate is zero false positives). (e) Sticky merges are recorded at the EDGE level ({from:[x], into} per edge) so chains collapse correctly through union-find on later runs; signal attribution for a collapsed merge is exact because confirmed pair edges can never chain with open-merge edges (pair members are rejected from the buckets). (f) The widened stage guard (candidates ∪ sticky work) keeps a sticky-only run reporting and deleting exactly like a candidate run; with no Phase 21 artifacts on disk every path is byte-identical to pre-Phase-21 (gate 14.4's byte-identity guard stays green — detection fires on no pre-existing fixture). (g) runId = the curation report's run timestamp (one timestamp per stage). (h) The abbreviation matcher bounds full names to capitalized words + a small connector list (for/i/og/af/the/of/and/…) so leading prose words never join the match. PRE-EXISTING TESTS TOUCHED: none. DEVIATIONS: none from the phase doc or canon beyond the recorded design decisions. LLM cost $0.00.
